content: Health can be improved by increasing knowledge, influencing motivation, and enhancing health literacy. This process may involve the communication of information about the determinants of health, individual risk factors, and the effective use of the healthcare system. It can also include task-based communication to support specific actions, such as participation in immunization and screening programs, adherence to prescribed medications, or the adoption of healthier behaviors. Additionally, it may involve skills-based communication to develop transferable skills that empower individuals to make autonomous decisions about their health and adapt to changing circumstances. This includes equipping people with the knowledge and skills necessary to address the determinants of health. Health literacy refers to the personal knowledge and competence that individuals accumulate through daily activities, social interactions, and intergenerational learning. This knowledge and competence are influenced by organizational structures and resources that enable individuals to access, understand, evaluate, and use information and services to promote and maintain their health and well-being, as well as that of those around them. Health promotion is defined as the process of enabling individuals to gain greater control over and improve their health. It extends beyond focusing solely on individual behaviors to encompass a wide range of social and environmental interventions. Ideally, health promotion activities are comprehensive and multifaceted, often framed within the context of prevention strategies for groups, communities, or populations. It also includes individual approaches, such as treatment and ongoing care. A health-promoting school is one that consistently strengthens its capacity to serve as a safe and healthy environment for teaching, learning, and working. This concept includes comprehensive school health, healthy learning environments, and schools that prioritize health. Implementation of health-promoting school initiatives involves a series of activities, including identifying issues, setting desired outcomes, planning, monitoring, collecting and using data, and collaborating with internal and external stakeholders. In schools, implementation is often a complex interaction between the characteristics of the education system, the implementers, and the organizational context. Indicators are variables used to monitor or evaluate measurable progress toward completing an activity, achieving an output, or meeting a goal or objective. These indicators can be categorized as input indicators (monitoring resources such as human and financial capital), process indicators (monitoring activities and their quality), output indicators (monitoring results such as service access and quality), outcome indicators (monitoring intermediate results at the population level), and impact indicators (monitoring long-term outcomes such as reductions in mortality and morbidity). In-service teachers are those who are registered and employed as teachers in schools, while pre-service teachers are students enrolled in initial educator preparation programs. Professional learning for teachers and school leaders involves both formal and informal experiences aimed at improving individual and collective professional practices. This learning is often measured by improvements in student learning, engagement, and well-being. Intersectoral collaboration refers to the working relationship between two or more sectors to achieve health and education outcomes in an effective, efficient, and sustainable manner. Knowledge translation involves the synthesis, exchange, and application of knowledge by relevant stakeholders to accelerate the benefits of global and local innovations in strengthening education systems and improving student health and well-being. A local community includes both the geographical community near a school and external organizations that engage with students or staff. These may include local government authorities, non-governmental organizations, faith-based organizations, private enterprises, community health services, and groups such as youth organizations and providers of organized sports, arts, and cultural activities. A logic model is a graphic representation of the relationships among goals, objectives, implementation strategies, activities, and their intended effects. Stakeholders are individuals, groups, or organizations with an interest in or who may be affected by the implementation of health-promoting school initiatives. These include students, parents, teachers, administrative staff, and school leaders. The concept of a whole-school approach extends beyond classroom teaching and learning to encompass all aspects of school life. This includes teaching content and methods, school governance, partnerships with the community, and campus and facility management. It is a cohesive, collective, and collaborative approach aimed at improving student learning, behavior, and well-being, as well as the conditions that support them. Every school should be a health-promoting school. No education system can be effective unless it promotes the health and well-being of its students, staff, and community. The COVID-19 pandemic has underscored the strong links between health and education. The health-promoting school approach, introduced over 25 years ago, has been globally promoted but has yet to achieve full implementation and sustainability at scale in most countries. This publication provides guidance for adapting and implementing global standards for health-promoting schools. It is based on an extensive review of global evidence on the barriers and enablers of implementation, maintenance, and scaling-up of the health-promoting school approach. It aims to guide stakeholders in understanding what should be done, how it should be done, and who should be involved in making every school a health-promoting school. Schools are increasingly recognized as critical settings for promoting the health, development, and well-being of children and adolescents. They support long-term educational attainment and contribute to the health and well-being of students, their families, and the local community. The interactive and mutually reinforcing relationship between health and education extends well beyond formal schooling. Supporting schools in promoting health while building the knowledge, skills, and competence of children and adolescents offers significant benefits for individuals, families, and communities. A health-promoting school is one that continuously strengthens its capacity as a healthy setting for living, learning, and working. This concept embodies a whole-school approach to promoting health and educational attainment by fostering physical, social-emotional, and psychological conditions conducive to health and positive educational outcomes. Health-promoting school initiatives and other whole-school approaches to supporting health in education have been implemented for decades. However, the global uptake and sustainability of these initiatives remain essential. Health-promoting education systems are necessary to institutionalize health promotion across all functions of the education system, including governance, resource allocation, professional development, information systems, and performance management. In 2018, WHO and UNESCO launched an initiative to make every school a health-promoting school and developed global standards and indicators for health-promoting schools. This initiative aims to support implementation by government departments, school staff, civil society organizations, and international partners. A standards-driven approach, including guidance for implementing health-promoting schools, is expected to strengthen whole-school approaches to health promotion worldwide. The global standards for health-promoting schools provide a vision in which all schools can enhance the health, well-being, and educational outcomes of their students and communities. This requires schools to adopt a whole-school approach to health promotion, integrating health into the culture, conditions, and curriculum of the school.
